hints.title: Team Member Tally Window Function
hints.text: Each employee belongs to a team. The team size is the total count of employees sharing that team_id.

hints.title: Partition By Team Identifier
hints.text: Use count(*) over (partition by team_id) to calculate the team size for every employee without collapsing rows.

hints.title: Team Size Blueprint
hints.text: select employee_id, count(*) over (partition by team_id) as team_size from Employee.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id) AS team_size
FROM Employee;
```

complexity.notes: Window partition counts execute in a single linear pass using an internal hash partition.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard GROUP BY collapses all team members into a single row, losing individual employee_id records.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window function avoids self-joining employee table back to a grouped team count subquery.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id).

solutions.code:
SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id) AS team_size
FROM Employee;
solutions.approach: Window Count Partition by Team ID

solutions.code:
SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY team_id) AS team_size
FROM Employee;

import pandas as pd

def team_size(employee: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    employee['team_size'] = employee.groupby('team_id')['employee_id'].transform('count')
    return employee[['employee_id', 'team_size']]
